daysAbroad.title: Schengen Tracker
daysAbroad.intro: Log where you are and when: ashore in a country, or signed on a vessel. Only you know when you sign on and off, so this is entered by hand.
daysAbroad.nowNone: No open stay. Tap Signed on or Add stay.

daysAbroad.countsSchengenHelp: Time on board a vessel in a Schengen port or its waters normally counts as time in the Schengen area. The EU Court of Justice has held that a seafarer on a ship moored in a Schengen port has not left the area (case C-341/18). Leave this on unless a border authority has told you otherwise.
daysAbroad.countsSchengenAtSeaHelp: Days at sea after leaving a Schengen port still count, because you have not left the Schengen area. Turn this off only if you cleared out with an exit check before sailing. Days at sea after a port outside the area never count.
daysAbroad.countsTaxHelp: Turn off to leave this stay out of the tax day counts, for example time on a foreign vessel that a country does not count.

schengen.disclaimer: Guidance, not legal advice. Entry and exit days both count. Days in Monaco, San Marino, the Vatican and Andorra are counted, and days in Gibraltar from 15 July 2026. Days at sea straight after a Schengen port count unless you turn that stay off. Days with nothing logged are treated as outside the area, so log every stay in the area. Time on a residence permit or long-stay visa does not count, so do not log it here. Check with the border authority if unsure.

tax.title: Tax days
tax.disclaimer: Guidance only, not tax advice. Day counts are only one part of tax residence: a home, family, work or main interests in a country can make you resident there with fewer days, and tax treaties can change the answer. Check with a tax adviser.
tax.none: No countries picked. Tap Choose countries.
tax.noRule: No day rule in the app for this country, so this is a plain count by calendar year.

noRuleNotes.NL: The Netherlands has no day-count test: residence depends on all your circumstances, so this is a plain count by calendar year. If you live on board a ship with a Dutch home port, the ship counts as the Netherlands when deciding where you live. If you leave and come back within a year without living elsewhere, you can be treated as resident the whole time.
noRuleNotes.BE: Belgium has no day-count test: you are resident if your home (domicile) is in Belgium or, without one, the seat of your wealth. Being on the National Register is presumed to mean your home is there unless you prove otherwise. The tax office treats moving between several countries as not settling abroad, so seafarers usually stay Belgian residents. This is a plain count by calendar year.
noRuleNotes.MC: Monaco has no personal income tax for most residents, so there is no day test and this is a plain count. French nationals living in Monaco are taxed by France unless they have lived in Monaco since 13 October 1957 or earlier.
noRuleNotes.PH: A Filipino seafarer on a ship engaged only in international trade is treated as an overseas worker and taxed only on income from the Philippines, with no day test, as long as you hold a valid OEC and seaman's book (SIRB). Other citizens working abroad need at least 183 days outside the Philippines in the year. This is a plain count by calendar year.

CY.title: I meet the 60-day rule
CY.help: At least 60 days in Cyprus; no more than 183 days in any one other country; work, a business or an office in Cyprus that does not end during the year; a home in Cyprus that you own or rent. Until 2025 you also had to be tax resident nowhere else.

AE.title: I meet the 90-day rule
AE.help: You hold a UAE residence permit, or are a UAE or GCC national, and you have a permanent home, a job or a business in the UAE. Then 90 days in 12 months makes you resident.

tax.nzVisitor: I qualify as a non-resident visitor
tax.nzVisitorHelp: From 1 April 2026: you arrived on or after that date, do not work for a New Zealand business, are not required to be in New Zealand for work, are there lawfully and are tax resident in another country. The 183-day rule then does not apply; more than 275 days in any 18 months makes you resident from day 276.
tax.esCertificate: I have a tax residence certificate from another country for {{year}} (trips away are then not added)
tax.countMidnight: Counts the days you are there at midnight. The day you leave does not count.
tax.countAnyPart: Any part of a day counts, so arrival and departure days both count.

count.midnight: Counts the days you are there at midnight. The day you leave does not count.
count.any_part: Any part of a day counts, so arrival and departure days both count.
count.overnight: A day counts if it includes a night in the country, so day trips do not count.
count.departure_out: The day you leave counts as a day outside and the day you arrive as a day in. A visit that starts and ends on one day counts.

tax.unrecorded_other: {{count}} days in this year have no stay logged.

notes.GB: Statutory Residence Test: 183 days or more in the UK in a tax year makes you UK resident. With fewer days you can still be resident through a UK home, full-time UK work or UK ties, and days you leave before midnight can count if you have 3 or more UK ties.
notes.US: Substantial presence test: 31 days this year and 183 days over 3 years (all of this year, a third of last year, a sixth of the year before). Days as regular crew of a foreign vessel travelling between the US and abroad may not count, but only if you do no other work in the US those days: check before turning those stays off. With fewer than 183 days this year, a closer connection to another country can still make you non-resident.
notes.AU: 183-day test: in Australia for more than half the income year (183 days, or 184 in a leap year) makes you resident, unless your usual home is overseas and you do not intend to live in Australia. Living in Australia or an Australian domicile can make you resident with fewer days.
notes.NZ: More than 183 days in New Zealand in any 12-month period makes you tax resident from the first of those days. A permanent place of abode in New Zealand makes you resident whatever the days. From 1 April 2026 some short-term visitors are treated as non-resident for up to 275 days in any 18 months: switch it on below if you qualify.
notes.ZA: Physical presence test: more than 91 days this tax year and in each of the 5 years before, and more than 915 days over those 5 years. If you ordinarily live in South Africa you are resident whatever the days.
notes.IE: 183 days in a tax year, or 280 days over this year and last. A year with 30 days or fewer does not count towards the 280, and you are not resident in that year under the 280-day test.
notes.CA: Staying 183 days or more in a calendar year can make you a deemed resident if you have no significant ties to Canada. If you do have significant ties (a home, a partner or dependants in Canada) you can be resident whatever the days.
notes.ES: More than 183 days in Spain in a calendar year. Days between two stays in Spain count as days in Spain, whether nothing is logged or you logged a trip away, unless you hold a tax residence certificate from another country; a single absence of more than 183 days is not added. Your main business or economic interests in Spain, or a spouse and young children living there, can also make you resident.
notes.FR: More than six months in France in a year usually makes it your main place of stay, but it is not an absolute test. Your home, job or main economic interests in France can also make you resident.
notes.IT: In Italy for most of the year (183 days, or 184 in a leap year). From 2024 physical presence alone can count. Your home, family ties or registration in Italy can also make you resident.
notes.DE: An unbroken stay of more than six months, even across the year end, makes Germany your habitual abode from the first day. This does not apply to purely private visits or holidays of up to a year. A home in Germany makes you resident whatever the days. Short breaks (home trips, leave, business trips) do not stop the stay; the law gives no limit, and the app joins stays across breaks of up to six weeks, counting the break days.
notes.HR: A permanent or connected stay of at least 183 days in Croatia, in one calendar year or across two, makes it your habitual residence. Short breaks of up to a year do not end the stay. The law does not say whether break days count, so the app counts only your days in Croatia towards the 183. It also does not say how part days count, so the app counts any part of a day. A home in Croatia that you own or have use of for at least 183 days makes you resident whatever your days abroad. The seafarer income exemption (183 days on ships in international traffic) is a separate rule.
notes.PL: More than 183 days in Poland in a tax year (calendar year). The days do not have to be in one stay. Your centre of personal or economic interests in Poland also makes you resident.
notes.PT: More than 183 days in Portugal in any 12 months that start or end in the year. A home kept as your habitual residence also makes you resident, and crew of ships run by a Portuguese company on 31 December are resident.
notes.GR: More than 183 days in Greece in total in any 12 months makes you resident from your first day there, for the year the 183 days are passed. Days abroad do not count. Days spent only on holiday or for medical treatment are left out, unless such a stay passes 365 days. Your permanent home or centre of vital interests in Greece also makes you resident.
notes.MT: Malta has no day test in law: residence depends on all the facts. The tax authority says more than 183 days in Malta in a year makes you resident for that year, so the app uses that as a guide. If you move to Malta to settle, you are resident from the day you arrive. Your home, ties and how often you visit also count. Malta does not say how part days count, so the app counts any part of a day.
notes.CY: More than 183 days in Cyprus in a calendar year. Under the 60-day rule, 60 days can be enough if you spent no more than 183 days in any one other country, work, run a business or hold an office in Cyprus all year and have a home there: switch it on below if that is you. Until 2025 you also had to be tax resident nowhere else.
notes.GI: At least 183 days in Gibraltar in a tax year (1 July to 30 June), or more than 300 days over three tax years in a row. The app flags every year in a three-year run that passes 300.
notes.AE: 183 days or more in the UAE in any 12 months in a row. 90 days can be enough if you hold a UAE residence permit (or are a UAE or GCC national) and have a home, job or business in the UAE: switch it on below if that is you.
notes.SE: A stay in Sweden of at least six months in a row makes you resident. Temporary breaks, such as visits home, do not end the stay and count towards the six months. The law gives no limit; the app treats a break as temporary when it is no longer than your stay in Sweden before or after it, and never over six months. A home in Sweden, or close ties after you leave, can also make you resident. A new rule (more than 160 days in a year) is planned from 2027.
notes.NO: More than 183 days in Norway in any 12 months, or more than 270 days in any 36 months. The days do not have to be in a row. You are resident from the year the count is passed.
notes.DK: A stay in Denmark of at least six months in a row makes you resident. Short holiday trips abroad do not end the stay and count towards the six months, but working abroad ends it, and so can frequent breaks. The law gives no limit; the app joins a break that is no longer than your stay before or after it, unless you logged time on board outside Denmark in it. A home in Denmark makes you resident whatever the days, and Danish citizens on ships with a Danish home port usually stay resident.

sed.title: UK Seafarers' Earnings Deduction
sed.intro: Checks the day tests only: 365 days or more, at least half of them outside the UK, with no UK visit over 183 days. A day abroad is a day you are outside the UK at midnight. Days with no stay logged count as UK days.
sed.current: Current period: {{start}} to {{end}}, {{days}} days ({{away}} away, {{uk}} in the UK).
sed.broken: More than 183 days in the UK since this period ended, so a new period starts with your next trip.
sed.disclaimer: Guidance only. Check with a tax adviser. SED has other conditions too, such as the type of ship and where the work is done.
